name: Old Town (Eski Mardin) around Cumhuriyet Meydani
tagline: The terraced stone heart of Mardin
description: The postcard core, where honey-coloured limestone houses cascade below the citadel around the main square and bazaar street. Boutique stone hotels, terrace cafes and craft shops fill the stepped lanes, with sweeping views over the Mesopotamian plain. Atmospheric but steep and touristy.
bestFor: Culture lovers, photographers and short-stay nomads wanting the classic Mardin experience
pros: Unbeatable heritage setting and terrace views
Best boutique hotels and laptop-friendly cafes
Everything walkable within the old town
cons: Steep stepped lanes are hard on luggage and knees
Busiest and priciest area during tourist season

name: Kasimiye and Zinciriye Madrasa Quarter
tagline: Monuments, quiet lanes and long views
description: The upper and eastern old-town area around the landmark Zinciriye and Kasimiye madrasas, full of courtyards, domes and stone detail. Quieter than the central bazaar, with a contemplative feel and some of the finest architecture and panoramas in the city.
bestFor: History buffs and slow travellers who want calm near the landmarks
pros: Surrounded by Mardin's finest historic monuments
Quieter and more contemplative than the main bazaar
Superb elevated views over the plain
cons: Steep climbs to reach the upper madrasas

name: Yenisehir (New Town)
description: The newer district below and beyond the old town, with wider streets, modern apartments, supermarkets, banks, hospitals and everyday services. Less picturesque but far more practical for longer stays, cheaper rents and flat, easy walking without the endless steps of the historic core.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads wanting affordability, services and level ground
pros: Cheaper rents than the restored old town
Full range of services, shops and healthcare
Flat streets and easier daily logistics
cons: Lacks the historic charm and views
Requires a dolmus or taxi up to the old town

name: Deyrulzafaran and Midyat side
description: The area east and southeast of the city toward the Deyrulzafaran Syriac Orthodox monastery and, further out, the stone town of Midyat in the Tur Abdin. Rural, deeply historic and rich in Syriac heritage, best reached by car for day trips or a quieter rural base.
vibe: Rural, spiritual, off the beaten path
bestFor: Culture seekers and those exploring Syriac heritage and Midyat
pros: Access to the Deyrulzafaran monastery and Tur Abdin
Rich Syriac history and stone architecture
cons: A car or driver is essentially required
Very limited nomad services and cafes
